newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler, SMH unveil Smart car, promise 10,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Daimler, SMH unveil Smart car, promise 10,000 jobs.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG and Swiss partner SMH on Thursday gave journalists a first glimpse of their "Smart" microcompact car and pledged the venture would create 10,000 jobs in total.
The unveiling of the Smart, geared for city driving and small enough to fit into a third of the parking space of a normal car, took place under strict security in a disused factory hall in Munich.

Cameras and recording equipment were banned at the world's first preview and the models on display very closely matched the final version which will hit showrooms in Europe in April 1998, company officials said.

The jobs will be created in France, where the car will be assembled, as well as among suppliers and dealers in Gemany and Switzerland, Daimler management board member Juergen Hubbert said at the first presentation worldwide of the car.
The car is being developed by Daimler's Mercedes-Benz AG unit and SMH, the parent company of watchmaker Swatch.
It will be launched on the European market in April 1998 and will be priced at 16,000 marks, company officials said.
A convertible version will follow in 1999, Hubbert said. The 1.5 billion-mark investment in the project should be recouped in six or seven years.
Hubbert said he did not expect rival manufacturers to launch a competing car yet. For the time being the competitors were waiting to see whether Daimler got "a bloody nose" with the venture, he said.
Smart will only be sold in Europe and will be available with three different engines -- diesel, petrol and a hybrid version which be partly be powered by electricity.
In 1998 Daimler and SMH plan to produce 100,000 cars at the plant in Hambach in Lorraine, France.

The petrol version of the car will use just under four litres of fuel per 100 kilometres and the diesel version will consume 3.42 litres making it the first three-litre car in mass production, Hubbert said.
The manufacturers pride themselves on the Smart's safety standards of the car which measures just 2.50 metres in length and is 1.45 metres wide.
The driver and passenger sit higher than usual and the car is fitted with so-called crash boxes at the front and rear which can be replaced cheaply after small accidents.
